A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SafeStyle research, with matching authors, research questions, and retained experiments. The complete main texts and appendices, including rendered figures and tables, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 32 LLMs across seven jailbreak benchmarks, controlled fine-tuning experiments, and SafeStyle safety and utility comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds natural instruction-tuning evaluations, news/legal style experiments, and appendix analyses including HumanEval results.

M1.justification: The core defense remains fine-tuning with 50 style-matched safety examples. Section 5.2 adds an adaptation for natural instruction data: extract styles using GPT-4o, sample ten bigrams according to frequency, and incorporate them into safety examples. This extends the augmentation procedure without changing the underlying training method.

E1.justification: v2 adds Dolly-15K instruction data, news/legal response-style conditions, and HumanEval programming evaluation. It also evaluates SafeStyle on natural Alpaca instructions; Alpaca itself, the seven jailbreak datasets, and AlpacaEval were already used in v1. These additions substantially broaden the evaluated data and task requirements.

E2.justification: Both Table 1 comparisons contain No Defense, Vanilla, PTST, SPPFT, Constrained, and Paraphrase against SafeStyle. v2 extends this same comparator set to its new style conditions and natural-data comparison in Table 2.

E3.justification: v2 adds a natural-data protocol using Dolly-15K and Alpaca-52K with GPT-4o responses, one training epoch for Alpaca-52K, and evaluation on original, untransformed queries. The equal four-style mixture and its averaged evaluation are removed. HumanEval Pass@1 and readability-change measurement are also added; the retained controlled experiments keep their stated settings.

E4.justification: Targeted extensions add a readability-based complexity analysis, news/legal tests of matched-style vulnerability, and news/legal safety-data alternatives in the existing style ablation. Appendix C.2 checks whether code-style tuning harms programming capability. The original attention, length, mixing-ratio, position, and safety-data-quantity analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both Section 4.1 descriptions specify three repetitions and reporting mean scores. Correlations with p-values and the existing distribution plots remain the reporting practice. The new complexity correlation adds a result, without a new uncertainty-estimation procedure or changed seed/run disclosure.

E6.justification: All shared Table 1 scores for list, poem, Shakespeare, and code match. v2 adds news/legal results and the natural-data Table 2, while removing mixture results. New Llama SafeStyle ASR changes are -0.045 on Dolly and -0.049 on Alpaca. Appendices add a complexity correlation of 0.078 and HumanEval Pass@1 of 72.6 before versus 73.1 after code-style tuning within v2. These are newly reported experiments, not performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs. The operational definitions of ASR inflation and attention difference are retained. The added readability-based empirical analysis does not introduce a formal theoretical result or derivation.

C1.justification: The three principal claims remain: style patterns inflate ASR, superficial style tuning increases matched-style vulnerability, and style-matched safety data mitigates that vulnerability while preserving utility. v2 updates the experimental scope in the abstract and introduction, providing broader evidence for these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains predefined styles as a control against noise, interprets natural-data results as evidence of robustness, and notes limited improvement headroom from low initial ASR. It drops the PTST/Constrained utility-failure hypotheses and the explicit limitation about unexplored styles beyond prefixes/suffixes. Attention-based interpretation caveats survive in Appendix A.2.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly documents the source safety corpus: 2,000 Anthropic red-team questions converted into instructions with GPT-3.5-turbo refusal responses. New tables illustrate style transformations. Reported hardware changes from four to eight NVIDIA A100 GPUs; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. The code-access statement remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 distinguishes benchmark-intrinsic style effects from engineered jailbreak transformations and discusses h4rm3l and Constitutional Classifiers. It adds journalism/legal, Dolly, HumanEval, readability, and safety-data references while removing mathematical-task and nuanced-style references. The overall alignment, safety-risk, and defense positioning remains.

P1.justification: The main progression from ASR inflation to style tuning to SafeStyle is retained. v2 revises introductory and related-work framing, moves detailed factor and utility discussion into subdivided appendices, adds a natural-data subsection, and replaces the closing Discussion with a shorter Conclusion.

P2.justification: The displays and layout are substantially reorganized. Figure 1 is redrawn; Figure 3 loses its length panel, which joins the expanded appendix Figure 7; the utility grid moves to Figure 9. Safety-style legends expand, Table 1 replaces mixture with news/legal columns, and new Table 2, Figure 8, and style-example tables accompany document-wide formatting changes.

improvement.justification: v1 validates the defense only on predefined styles and their synthetic mixture. v2 specifies an adaptation for naturally occurring styles and evaluates it on Dolly and Alpaca across the retained models and baselines (Sections 5.2–5.4, Table 2), addressing an important applicability gap. Additional robustness and programming-utility checks strengthen the evidence. Removing mixture results and shortening explicit limitations are costs, but the new validation provides a substantial net quality gain.
